title: Daniel's 70 Weeks
description:
Daniel 540 BC what was going to happen to Jerusalem. 

1. Rebuilding Jerusalem would take 49 years
2.The Messiah comes after another 434 years and then Jerusalem with be destroyed again.
3. Great tribulation will happen in Jerusalem for 7 years at some time in the future.

That is a total 490 years which Daniel expressed in multiples of 7's weeks (like we my talk of decades) and is where 70 weeks (of 7 years comes from).

Repentance
description: turning from sin to God, involving a change of mind, confession, and changed behavior.

title: What is the Gospel?
description: The Good News of the Kingdom of God

title: The Kingdom of God is at hand
Thought
description: The inner process of repentance, beginning with God revealing Himself, then conviction of specific sins, godly sorrow, and a deliberate shift to agree with God’s verdict.

title: Revelation of God
description: God making Himself known through creation, conscience, and the preached word, before any conviction can take hold.

title: Conviction
description: the Spirit exposing specific sins, revealing God’s holiness, your sinfulness, and even the offensiveness of your good deeds.

title: Your sinfulness
description: Realizing you are worse than thought

title: Godly sorrow
description: grief that you’ve offended God Himself, distinct from regret over consequences.

title: Contrast with regret
description: Regret is about self; sorrow is Godward

title: Change of mind
description: metanoia — rethinking your view of God as better than you imagined and yourself as worse.

title: Word
description: confessing sins by name, taking ownership, and renouncing them.

title: Specific confession
description: naming individual sins rather than generalizing, owning your choices without excuses.

title: Renunciation
description: verbally declaring you are finished with the sin and will not return to it.

title: Deed
description: proving repentance through actions that match it, including restitution and producing fruit.

title: Fruit of repentance
description: deeds that demonstrate the repentance is real, such as correcting wrongs and walking in freedom.

title: Helping someone repent
description: guiding another person through the process with seriousness, specificity, and moral clarity.

title: Be sensible
description: Moral guilt not psychological; not everything fixable

title: Faith
description: trusting Jesus personally as Savior and Lord, relying on His death and resurrection, committing your life to Him, and living in ongoing relationship with Him.

title: Historical
description: the factual foundation — Jesus died, was buried, and rose with a body.

title: Personal
description: faith directed at Jesus Himself, not merely about Him — trusting and relating to Him as a living friend.

title: Trust
description: Rely on Him as Saviour and Lord

title: Verbal
description: expressing faith outwardly by praying to Jesus and confessing Him.

title: Practical
description: faith taking action, risking steps, and producing deeds, since faith without works is dead.

title: Continual
description: faith as lifelong trust, sustained through trials and not a one-time moment.

title: Water Baptism
description: immersion in water as commanded by Jesus, signifying cleansing from sin, burial with Christ, and rising to new life.

title: Command
description: Jesus’ direct instruction to baptize all disciples.

title: Meaning
description: baptism as both a bath that washes away sins and a burial that unites you with Christ’s death and resurrection.

title: Purpose
description: baptism for the remission of sins, salvation, and deliverance from Satan’s territory.

title: Practice
description: the uniform New Testament pattern of baptizing believers, with no unbaptized believers recorded.

title: Receive the Holy Spirit
description: the definite reception of the Spirit Himself as a free gift, given to all who repent and are baptized, often with signs following.

title: Experience
description: a real, observable reception, normally through laying on of hands and frequently accompanied by manifestations.

title: Filling
description: the Spirit given for power and future service, sought by asking.

title: Distinction from water
description: water cleanses the past; the Spirit fills for the future, received into an empty and clean vessel.

title: By faith
description: the Spirit received through faith, not earned by works.
